column3: “Like” makes the dove image an explicit comparison; the Hebrew says the eyes “are doves.”
“Each has its twin” replaces the picture of all bearing twins; “newly” is added.
“Of stones” specifies what the rows consist of.
The first “two,” before “breasts,” is not expressed separately.
“Before” replaces “until,” and “breaks” interprets the image of the day breathing.
“One glance” replaces “one of your eyes,” and “one jewel” replaces a necklace.
“Love” renders the plural expressions of love collectively.
“Sweetness like the honeycomb” replaces the honey dripping from the lips.
“You are” is supplied; “garden” is singular where the Hebrew has “gardens.” “Fresh water” renders “living water.”
“Breathe on my garden” replaces the causative request to make the garden breathe; “spread the fragrance” interprets the spices flowing. “Taste” replaces “eat.”
